highlights.title: Jensen Huang's Nvidia return shows the U.S.-China AI race is about more than chips
highlights.description: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO demonstrates that the U.S.-China artificial intelligence race is not just about semiconductors, but tech talent too.

highlights.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to U.S. industrial might — not a champion
highlights.description: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.

highlights.title: Op-ed: Trump’s Nvidia board intervention put a price on national security. Our adversaries will take note
highlights.description: President Trump's decision to force Nvidia's board to bring back Jensen Huang as CEO is exactly what Beijing, Tehran, and Moscow would want to see.

highlights.title: Trump reportedly says pardoning Jensen Huang is ‘an option’
highlights.description: Huang faces ongoing questions about his relationship with Alice Huang, an executive with alleged ties to Chinese intelligence who previously worked for a company that has been accused of illegally diverting Nvidia chips to China.

ai.title: Epochal launches with $100M to help developers train predictive AI models
ai.description: Artificial intelligence tooling startup Epochal AI Inc. launched today with $100 million in funding. The capital was provided by Chief Executive Officer Guodong Zhang, a machine learning researcher who earlier co-founded xAI Corp. He established Epochal earlier this year with two other xAI co-founders, Zihang Dai and Manuel Kroiss. devices.title: Huawei’s home-grown HarmonyOS passes 100 million device mark in ‘landmark moment’
devices.description: Huawei Technologies has announced that HarmonyOS, its home-grown, Android-free operating system, has surpassed 100 million installations, marking a milestone in its effort to build a software ecosystem independent of Google’s mobile services amid US-led sanctions. The Shenzhen-based firm said the total was reached this month across smartphones, tablets and personal computers running HarmonyOS 5, 6 and 7. Its ecosystem now offered more than 460,000 apps and services from over 12 million...
